messages.subject_clean: error: tip range not allowed in states_list
messages.body_plain:

I've never seen this error, but it could be because you have tips with the same name. Did you have duplicated names in your January dataset? CR for example appears twice.

Julia

messages.subject: Re: max_range_size Fatal Error
messages.body_plain:
Hi Sébastien,

with max_range = 3 you can only estimate ranges of up to 3 areas. If one of your species has a range of 6, then your max range has to be at least 6, otherwise the model cannot even estimate that input range.

I'll also add that 10 areas for a 16-tip tree is too much. At times, we might want to be as precise as possible and define many areas to represent in detail the distribution of a set of species, but this results in a large number of areas that does not necessarily help answering a question.

Julia

On Wednesday, February 23, 2022 at 4:50:24 PM UTC+1 mirolo.s...@gmail.com wrote:
> Hi Nick and everyone,
>
> I'm new to BioGeoBEARS and ancestral area reconstruction (ancestral range estimation, I did my research) in general. I'm trying to analyse a small dataset of 16 species on 10 different areas. As the analysis takes ages to run with that many areas, I would like to set the max_range_size to 3 or 4 but it gives me this error message when I check the parameters with check_BioGeoBEARS_run(BioGeoBEARS_run_object) :
>
> FATAL ERROR in inputs: max_tipsize=6 > inputs$max_range_size=3
>
> I understand that it's because one of my species have a present range of 6 areas but I don't get why it's a problem to constrain the reconstruction. I'm working on bryophytes, a large geographic range is almost the rule. Is there any way to run the analysis without decreasing the number of areas?
>
> Very best,
> Sébastien

messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Re: max_range_size Fatal Error
messages.body_plain:
Yep that's it Julia -- if max_range_size=3, then all tips must be 3 areas or less.

(You could, if you want, use a manual_states_list and time-stratify it to allow 6-area ranges from e.g. 0-1 million years ago, and then only 3-area ranges before that, but then you'd have to

(a) justify this decision, this time-point cutoff, etc.
(b) do the setup, which is complex, but based on: http://phylo.wikidot.com/example-biogeobears-scripts#modified_states_stratified

Thanks for the answer, I've been travelling!

Cheers,
Nick

(PS 10 areas for a 16-tip tree is physically possible on the computer,

messages.subject: Re: running SSE_simtrait simulation
messages.body_plain:
Dear colleagues,
it has been impossible to run the routine   "run_SSE_simtrait_v2.R" provided by Kristina Klaus. I have changed the BioGeoBEARS_run_object with DIVALIKE + j parameters since it is my best model. I always get this error message:

Error in modify_Qmat_with_trait(Qmat = NULL, BioGeoBEARS_run_object = BioGeoBEARS_run_object,  :
  argument "numstates_geogtrait" is missing, with no default"

Apparently, neither the original Klaus' routine is correctly running. Does anyone have some idea about the problem?

My best regards,
José Ricardo.

>   argument "numstates_geogtrait" is missing, with no default
>
>
> Besides when I put my own traits, I have also an error. It seems that the tip labels are not matching. I have noticed that the routine of Kristina Klaus (Podocarpaceae) has no tree, but it seems that it could be possible. Have anyone tried to run that routine?
> My best regards,
> José Ricardo.

messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Re: running SSE_simtrait simulation
messages.body_plain:
Hi!  Apologies for missing this earlier -- some other part of the code probably changed since the analysis was run for the Klaus & Matzke paper.  I added a line to the modify_Qmat_with_trait() function, and posted it to GitHub, this seems to fix the issue.

I suggest:

1. Reinstall from GitHub: https://github.com/nmatzke/BioGeoBEARS

library(devtools)
devtools::install_github(repo="nmatzke/BioGeoBEARS")

2. Restart R

3. Run the attached script (simplified from the Supp. Mat version), making sure to
(a) set the location of master_wd somewhere sensible on your machine
(b) create a "sims" directory inside of that directory

...and it should work!  This is a 4-area, 2-trait simulation, followed by inference under a variety of models.

Cheers,
Nick
